analysis.explanation: The Random Forest classified this binary as malware with probability 1.0000, and all 20 top n-grams have positive SHAP contributions (+0.0087 to +0.0204), so none of the leading features argue against cryptojacking. The evidence shows no function names or API calls, so my interpretation rests only on the mnemonic n-gram patterns and their SHAP values. Several n-grams are consistent with the bit-manipulation and SIMD work typical of hashing or proof-of-work code. ROL ADD (+0.0124) and MOV ROL (+0.0121) suggest rotate-and-add mixing rounds. MOV SHRD (+0.0103) and SHRD BT (+0.0092) suggest multi-word shifts and bit tests, as in large-integer or 128/256-bit arithmetic. PXOR PXOR (+0.0108), PXOR MOVDQA (+0.0101), MOVDQA PAND (+0.0102), MOVDQA MOVAPS (+0.0141) and LEA MOVDQA (+0.0087) indicate SSE-based XOR, mask and move sequences. MOVDQA PAND is fairly frequent (0.0226), which suggests the SIMD logic is a substantive part of the code. Other n-grams (POP SUB, CALL PUSH, PUSH RET, POP PUSH, POP CALL, POP XOR, MOV RET, LEA JC, DEC JZ) are generic control-flow and stack patterns. They carry high SHAP weight but are individually non-specific; their rarity (frequency about 0.000124 to 0.000247) may reflect unusual stack manipulation or obfuscation, but this cannot be confirmed from the evidence. MOV MOVZX (0.0578) and ADD MOVZX (0.0164) are the most frequent, consistent with byte-level table lookups or data processing. No single n-gram is conclusive, but the model's maximal confidence and the combination of rotate, wide shift, and SIMD XOR/AND patterns make a high-confidence cryptojacking call reasonable.
